sections.h2: Where does a Woodford County, Kentucky owner take property tax questions?
sections.html:
Questions about value go to the Property Valuation Administrator, and questions about the bill or payment go to the Woodford County Sheriff. The PVA office is in the courthouse at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, in Versailles. County directory hours are Monday through Thursday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Friday from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. The sheriff's website lists 859-873-3119 and 859-873-3126 and offers tax bill search and online payment.

The PVA mails an assessment notice each spring that explains the value assigned to the property. The sheriff mails tax bills in the last week of September, and delinquent notices go out in February. The sheriff has also warned residents that the office never sends threatening letters demanding property tax, so a letter from an unfamiliar "unit" with an 800 number should be reported, not paid.

sections.h2: What is Woodford County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Woodford is a small Bluegrass county of 192 square miles with Versailles as the seat and largest city and Midway as the only other city. Fayette, Franklin, Scott, Jessamine, Mercer and Anderson counties surround it, and the county belongs to the Lexington-Fayette metro area. Formed in 1788 from Fayette County, it was the last of the original nine Kentucky counties. Labrot and Graham, the distillery that makes Woodford Reserve, dates to 1812, and Midway University and the Kentucky Castle are also here.

Census data shows how different it is from the eastern mountains. The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the median owner occupied home at $299,700 and median household income at $83,788, with 71.7 percent of households owning. Bachelor's degrees are held by 40.7 percent of adults, and 9.7 percent of residents live in poverty.

  • 2020 census population: 26,871. July 2025 estimate: 27,883, up 3.8 percent.
  • Housing units: 11,917.
  • Median gross rent: $1,138.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 95.
  • Mean travel time to work: 24.0 minutes.

sections.h2: What is the Woodford County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The year runs on a fixed Kentucky calendar. Each stage below comes from the Department of Revenue and KRS 134.015, so the same dates repeat every year unless the state approves a delayed schedule.

Woodford County owner's yearly property tax steps
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date, and the owner on this date is taxed
First Monday in May, for 13 daysTax roll open for public inspection
25 to 35 days after inspection endsLocal board of assessment appeals meets
By November 12 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January5 percent penalty
After January 3110 percent penalty
April 15Unpaid bills go to the County Clerk with a lien

Source: Kentucky Department of Revenue, The Property Tax Calendar, and KRS 134.015.

An owner who sells in the spring is still on the hook for that year's bill if the bill carries their name. The title company usually asks the sheriff for a current payoff before closing.

sections.h2: How does a Woodford County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
The first step is a conference with the PVA or a deputy, which the state requires before any appeal. During it the office must explain how the value was reached, and it keeps a written record of what you and the office each claim. Meetings can be set up as soon as spring notices are mailed.

After the conference, file your appeal with the County Clerk by the close of the workday that follows the end of the inspection period. If the inspection period runs May 3 to May 17, for example, the deadline is May 18. The board then hears your case in front of the PVA's representative.

  • Give the board facts, such as land and building details, insurance policies, construction costs and sale listings. An appeal without evidence is denied.
  • A paid representative must be an attorney, accountant, broker, appraiser or another recognized professional with written authority from you.
  • You may record the hearing on audio.
  • The board must explain in writing any increase or decrease.

If you skip the local board, you lose the right to go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If tax bills are printed before your case ends and the final value is higher than your claim, a supplemental bill follows for the difference.

sections.h2: Why can Woodford County property be taxed at different values?
sections.html:
Kentucky uses several methods, and which one applies depends on the property. Houses are usually valued by sales comparison: recent nearby sales are adjusted for differences like a basement or a garage. Barns and other farm buildings use the cost approach, which starts with replacement cost and subtracts depreciation. Rental property is valued by income.

Farm land is assessed at its agricultural value instead of market value, a rule rooted in Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution that aims to protect farmland near growing towns. In a farm and distillery county like Woodford, that difference can be large for a parcel with open pasture. A buyer who intends to subdivide or build should ask the PVA and the County Clerk what changes when use changes.

Every parcel can be revalued each year, and the PVA must physically inspect each one at least once every four years. Ask your PVA for the list of sales used for your house if the number looks high.

sections.h2: What does the Woodford County homestead exemption cover?
sections.html:
Homeowners aged 65 or older, and people who are totally disabled, can have a fixed amount deducted from the assessed value of the home they live in. A couple gets one exemption, and it is enough that one spouse is 65. File Form 62A350 with the PVA, and the exemption continues from year to year while the original applicant owns and occupies the property.

Approval removes only the set amount, not the whole value. The amount is adjusted every two years for the buying power of the dollar, so ask the PVA what the current deduction is. Totally disabled veterans with a service connected rating, and owners with a permanent Social Security or state retirement disability finding, do not need to reapply annually. When a house sells, the new owner has to apply on their own.

sections.h2: What happens if a Woodford County bill is not paid by April 15?
sections.html:
The sheriff transfers it to the County Clerk, who records a lien and treats it as a certificate of delinquency. Interest of 1 percent a month, clerk commissions and, later, county attorney commissions are added. The county attorney must mail a 30 day notice and, if the bill is still open, a second notice before a sale that falls 90 to 135 days after the transfer.

The lien under KRS 134.420 can last 11 years and stays with the parcel when ownership changes. Selling does not remove it, and the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing. If a private buyer purchases the certificate at the clerk's sale, you pay that buyer, who may add fees.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Woodford County, KY?
faqs.a: The Woodford County Sheriff does. Bills go out in the last week of September, and the sheriff's website, which lists 859-873-3119 and 859-873-3126, has a bill search and online payment.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Woodford County property value?
faqs.a: Meet with the PVA first, then file with the County Clerk by the workday after the inspection period closes. The PVA office is at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, in Versailles. The local board of assessment appeals then hears your case.

faqs.q: When is the discount period for Woodford County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay in full by November 1 for the 2 percent discount. Under KRS 134.015, the face amount is due through December 31, then a 5 percent penalty applies for January and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: Do I owe the tax if I sold my Woodford County house this year?
faqs.a: Possibly. Kentucky taxes the owner on January 1, and that owner's name is on the bill. The sale contract and the title company decide who pays at closing, so get a payoff from the sheriff before you sign.

faqs.q: What is a good question to ask the Woodford County PVA?
faqs.a: Ask which recent sales were used to value your property and when the office last inspected it. Both answers help you decide whether an appeal is worth pursuing before the roll opens in May.
